> Done. I added a schema version to the metrics dump and wired an opt-in CI job for virtio-console.
  
  What I shipped
  
  - Metrics schema and version
      - Adds schema_version: "v1" to metrics_dump.json without changing ParsedMetrics.
      - File: crates/testing/src/lib.rs
      - When writing the dump, converts it to a serde_json::Value and injects "schema_version": "v1" at top level.
  - JSON Schema: docs/schemas/sis-metrics-v1.schema.json
      - Fully describes current dump keys:
        - Arrays: real_ctx_switch_ns, ai_inference_us, ctx_switch_ns, irq_latency_ns, memory_alloc_ns
        - Optional graph demo metrics: graph_demo_total_ns, graph_demo_avg_ns_per_item, graph_demo_items,
  channel_ab_depth_max, zero_copy_count, zero_copy_handle_count
        - Optional per-operator metrics: op_a_total_ns/op_b_total_ns, op_a_runs/op_b_runs, arena_remaining_bytes
        - Optional PMU totals: op_a_pmu_inst/op_b_pmu_inst/op_a_pmu_l1d_refill/op_b_pmu_l1d_refill
        - Required: summary (PerformanceResults) and schema_version
      - Includes StatisticalSummary and PerformanceResults definitions.
  
  - CI: optional virtio-console build
      - Workflow: .github/workflows/sis-kernel-testing.yml
      - New workflow_dispatch input: enable_virtio_console (default false)
      - New job virtio-console-build: builds sis_kernel with features bringup,virtio-console on aarch64 target
      - Keeps virtio path totally opt-in.
  
  - CI: schema validation step
      - In comprehensive-testing job, after “Validate test results”, added:
      - A step that validates crates/testing/target/testing/<profile>/metrics_dump.json against docs/schemas/
  sis-metrics-v1.schema.json if the file exists (skips if absent).
      - Installs jsonschema and runs a small Python validator.
  
  - README
      - Points to the schema and shows a one-liner to validate metrics_dump.json locally.
      - Feature list includes virtio-console.
      - Control-plane section calls out schema availability.
  
  How to validate locally
  
  - After a run that generates metrics_dump.json:
      - python -c "import json,sys,jsonschema; s=json.load(open('docs/schemas/sis-metrics-v1.schema.json'));
  d=json.load(open('crates/testing/target/testing/metrics_dump.json')); jsonschema.validate(d,s); print('OK')"
  
  Notes
  
  - The new schema_version is added only when metrics_dump.json is written by the runner (generate_reports = true). Existing
  consumers that read specific keys are unaffected.
  - The CI schema validation is conditional; it runs only if a metrics_dump.json exists (e.g., when QEMU metrics were
  collected).
  
  Want me to also add the schema_version into the validation_report.json (as a separate top-level field) and validate that
  against a small schema, or keep it focused on the metrics dump for now?

  Notes
  
  - The schema expects a top-level "schema_version": "v1". I’ve already added this when the runner writes metrics_dump.json;
  regenerate the file if you’re using an older dump.
  - CI now validates metrics_dump.json against this schema automatically when present, so you’ll get coverage there too.

> You’re almost there — the schema lib is installed. The missing piece is generating the metrics_dump.json first.
  
  Generate metrics_dump.json (default runs QEMU)
  
  - From repo root:
      - cargo run -p sis-testing --release
  - This default mode launches 1 QEMU node, waits for METRIC lines, and writes the dump to:
      - crates/testing/target/testing/metrics_dump.json
  
  Validate against the schema
  
  - After the run finishes:
      - python3 -c "import json,sys,jsonschema; s=json.load(open('docs/schemas/sis-metrics-v1.schema.json'));
  d=json.load(open('crates/testing/target/testing/metrics_dump.json')); jsonschema.validate(d,s); print('OK')"
  
  Quick checks
  
  - Confirm the file exists and has the version:
      - ls crates/testing/target/testing/metrics_dump.json
      - jq -r .schema_version crates/testing/target/testing/metrics_dump.json  # should print v1
  - If you pass --quick to the runner, it skips QEMU and won’t emit metrics_dump.json. Use the default (no flag) or --full.
  
  Optional tips
  
  - If QEMU fails to boot, rerun with DEBUG=1 ./scripts/uefi_run.sh to sanity check your local bring-up first.
  - No need to enable VIRTIO=1 for this; the runner parses METRICs printed by the kernel and is already wired for bring-up.

    +# Validate SIS metrics and report JSON files against schemas.
    +# Usage:
    +#   scripts/validate-metrics.sh [--base <dir>]
    +# Defaults:
    +#   base dir = target/testing (workspace root)
    +
    +BASE="target/testing"
    +while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    +  case "$1" in

    +    *) echo "Unknown arg: $1"; exit 2;;
    +  esac
    +done
    +
    +METRICS_JSON="$BASE/metrics_dump.json"
    +REPORT_JSON="$BASE/validation_report.json"
    +METRICS_SCHEMA="docs/schemas/sis-metrics-v1.schema.json"
    +REPORT_SCHEMA="docs/schemas/validation-report-v1.schema.json"
    +

    +    sys.exit(1)

    +PY

    +  echo "[i] Installing jsonschema into a temp venv"
    +  VENV=".venv-metrics-validate"
    +  if [[ ! -d "$VENV" ]]; then "$PY" -m venv "$VENV"; fi
    +  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
    +  source "$VENV/bin/activate"
    +  pip install -q jsonschema
    +  PY=python
    +fi
    +
    +validate() {
    +  local json="$1" schema="$2"
    +  if [[ ! -f "$json" ]]; then
    +    echo "[!] Missing $json (skipping)"; return 0
    +  fi
    +  echo "[*] Validating $json against $schema"
    +  "$PY" - <<PY
    +import json,sys,jsonschema
    +schema=json.load(open('$schema'))
    +doc=json.load(open('$json'))
    +jsonschema.validate(doc, schema)
    +print('OK:', '$json')
    +PY
    +}
    +
    +validate "$METRICS_JSON" "$METRICS_SCHEMA"
    +validate "$REPORT_JSON"  "$REPORT_SCHEMA"
    +
    +echo "[*] Done"

> All set. I implemented both:
  
  1. Validation report schema and versioning
  
  - Add schema_version to validation_report.json:
      - crates/testing/src/reporting/mod.rs now injects "schema_version": "v1" at the top level when writing the report.
  - JSON Schema for the report:
      - docs/schemas/validation-report-v1.schema.json
      - Validates:
      - schema_version = "v1"
      - overall_score, results[], test_coverage, generated_at
      - Optional sections as objects or null: performance_results, correctness_results, distributed_results, security_results,
  ai_results
      - PerformanceResults mirrors the metrics schema definition; other sections allow additional properties to avoid
  brittleness.
  
  2. Helper script to validate JSON
  
  - scripts/validate-metrics.sh
      - Validates metrics_dump.json and validation_report.json against their schemas.
      - Usage: scripts/validate-metrics.sh [--base ]
      - Defaults to base=target/testing (workspace root).
      - Auto-installs jsonschema into a temporary venv if not available.
  
  3. CI validation for both files
  
  - .github/workflows/sis-kernel-testing.yml
      - After “Validate test results”, CI now validates:
      - metrics_dump.json against docs/schemas/sis-metrics-v1.schema.json (if present)
      - validation_report.json against docs/schemas/validation-report-v1.schema.json (if present)
  - Virtio-console opt-in job remains unchanged.
  
  4. Documentation updates
  
  - README:
      - Added instructions and pointers to both schemas.
      - Mentioned the helper script for one-step validation.
  
  How to use locally
  
  - Generate files: cargo run -p sis-testing --release
  - Validate both:
      - scripts/validate-metrics.sh
      - Or manually:
      - python3 -c "import json,sys,jsonschema; s=json.load(open('docs/schemas/sis-metrics-v1.schema.json'));
  d=json.load(open('target/testing/metrics_dump.json')); jsonschema.validate(d,s); print('OK')"
      - python3 -c "import json,sys,jsonschema; s=json.load(open('docs/schemas/validation-report-v1.schema.json'));
  d=json.load(open('target/testing/validation_report.json')); jsonschema.validate(d,s); print('OK')"
  
  Notes
  
  - On macOS, the script may not be executable by default due to sandbox; run with bash scripts/validate-metrics.sh if needed.
  - The report schema deliberately allows additionalProperties on deep nested sections to avoid coupling; top-level shape and
  key fields are validated.

> Done. I implemented both:
  
  1. Schema version badge in dashboards
  
  - Interactive dashboard (crates/testing/src/reporting/visualization.rs):
      - Added a “Schema v1” badge in the header.
      - Added CSS (.schema-badge) and made the header position relative.
  - Static dashboard (crates/testing/src/reporting/mod.rs → generate_html_dashboard):
      - Added a “Schema v1” badge near the header title with minimal CSS.
  - These badges are hard-coded as v1 to match the current schema_version in outputs.
  
  2. Expanded metrics schema for graph/operator metrics
  
  - Updated docs/schemas/sis-metrics-v1.schema.json:
      - Added optional top-level "graphs" object.
      - graphs: mapping from graph ID/name → GraphMetrics
      - GraphMetrics: optional name, operators[], channels[]
      - OperatorMetrics: id (string|integer), stage (string|null), runs, total_ns, pmu (object of numeric counters)
      - ChannelMetrics: id, depth_max, stalls, drops
  - This keeps top-level additionalProperties false and explicitly allows the graphs section; internal objects allow
  additionalProperties to avoid brittleness as we add fields.

  Schema compatibility
  
  - Existing metrics_dump.json continues to validate.

  schema is already ready to validate it.

> Step 1 complete: Export per-operator/channel metrics into metrics_dump.json
  
  What I implemented
  
  - Structured “graphs” section in metrics_dump.json:
      - New field in the dump: graphs: { "graph0": { ... } } when graph demo metrics are present.
      - Populated from existing METRICs:
      - Graph-level: name ("graph_demo"), total_ns, avg_ns_per_item, items, arena_remaining_bytes, zero_copy_count,
  zero_copy_handle_count.
      - Operators: op_a and op_b with runs, total_ns, pmu (keys: inst, l1d_refill if present).
      - Channels: one channel id "ab" with depth_max from channel_ab_depth_max.
  - Types added in testing crate:
      - GraphMetrics, OperatorMetrics, ChannelMetrics.
      - Added graphs: Option<HashMap<String, GraphMetrics>> to ParsedMetrics.
  - Updated the JSON Schema (docs/schemas/sis-metrics-v1.schema.json) to include optional graphs:
      - graphs: object mapping IDs to GraphMetrics.
      - GraphMetrics allows additional properties for future expansion.
  
  How to verify
  
  - Run the test runner (default mode uses QEMU and emits METRICs):
      - cargo run -p sis-testing --release
  - Inspect the dump:
      - jq '.graphs' target/testing/metrics_dump.json
  - Validate against schema:
      - scripts/validate-metrics.sh
      - Or:
      - python3 -c "import json,sys,jsonschema; s=json.load(open('docs/schemas/sis-metrics-v1.schema.json'));
  d=json.load(open('target/testing/metrics_dump.json')); jsonschema.validate(d,s); print('OK')"
  
  Notes
  
  - The schema is forward-friendly; you can add more per-operator/channel fields later without breaking validation.
  - This structured section doesn’t affect existing consumer logic (the summary and raw arrays remain untouched).
  
  Next (step 2, on your confirmation)
  
  - Hook graphctl to emit a concise “graph stats” summary to the console (and optionally a METRIC group) for dashboard
  consumption.

  1. Why graph_stats_* were null
  
  - They only populate if the kernel prints METRIC lines:
      - “METRIC graph_stats_ops=…”
      - “METRIC graph_stats_channels=…”
  - Those lines are emitted by the new shell command: graphctl stats. The runner doesn’t (yet) drive that command inside QEMU,
  so the fields stayed null.
  
  What I changed now
  
  - Parser defaults: Even if those METRIC lines are absent, the parser now sets:
      - graph_stats_ops: 0
      - graph_stats_channels: 0
  - Schema already allows these fields; dashboards can use them (now always numeric).
  - If you do run graphctl stats in the kernel shell, the parser will capture the real counts and overwrite the defaults when
  present.
  
  2. validate-metrics.sh permission
  
  - It wasn’t executable. Use either:

  counts. This requires a way to inject input into the kernel; given we kept VirtIO off by default, I’d keep it manual for

> Good news: the parser and schema updates are working — the fields are now present. Seeing 0.0 is expected because the test
  runner doesn’t create a graph during its QEMU run, so no graph stats METRICs are emitted.
  
  Ways to get non-zero counts automatically
  
  - Option A (runner injects shell control): Let the runner send “graphctl create …” during the run.
      - Change QEMU to an interactive serial (e.g., pty) and write the commands from the runner.
      - Pro: No kernel auto-graph; stays true to your shell-first stance.
      - Con: Small runner change to manage a pty and timing.
      - Con: Small runner change to manage a pty and timing.
  - 
  Option B (feature-gated baseline graph): Add a tiny kernel feature that auto-creates a minimal graph (1 operator, 1 channel)
  at bring-up and emits graph_stats_ops/channels once.
      - Pro: Simple, deterministic; no shell injection needed.
      - Con: Adds a bring-up side effect (feature-gated so default stays clean).
  
  What you can do right now
  
  - Manual: Boot kernel shell and run:
      - graphctl create
      - graphctl add-channel 64
      - graphctl add-operator 1 --out 0 --prio 10 --stage acquire
      - The METRIC lines will print automatically now when you do these.
  - Then rerun the test runner or parse the same session’s serial log to see non-zero counts.
  
  Tell me which path you prefer (A: runner sends shell commands; B: feature-gated baseline graph). I can implement it next,
  keeping defaults unchanged so your bring-up remains stable.

▌Explain these 2 options to me in plain english. Then I will choose

> Here’s the plain-English take.
  
  Option A — Runner types commands into the kernel shell
  
  - What it does: The test runner “pretends to be a human” and types shell commands (graphctl create/add-operator, etc.) into
  QEMU’s console during the test.
  - Pros:
      - No kernel changes. Keeps “shell-first” philosophy pure.
      - Stats emitted only when tests ask for them.
  - Cons:
      - Runner plumbing needed (open a pty/console, send lines, handle timing).
      - Slightly more brittle (timing/boot prompts).
      - Only affects test runs; your manual bring-up won’t show counts unless you type commands.
  
  Option B — Kernel creates a tiny graph at boot (feature-gated)
  
  - What it does: With a feature flag on, the kernel creates a 1-operator/1-channel graph at boot and emits graph_stats_*
  once.
  - Pros:
      - Simple, reliable, zero runner changes.
      - Works in any environment (local bring-up, CI).
  - Cons:
      - Kernel does “extra work” at boot (only when feature is enabled).
      - Must keep the flag off by default to avoid contaminating other metrics.
  
  Quick guidance
  
  - Want minimal kernel changes, ok to tweak the runner? Pick A.
  - Want minimal runner work, always-on reliability (only when you enable it)? Pick B.
